item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('README.md');s=p.read_text()
anchor='## Unreleased Must increment: trusted Keeper/stream lifecycle\\n'
section='''## Unreleased second Must: Send Off service and verified raid foundations

This second increment is separate from the reviewed lifecycle increment and is **not deployed**. The deployed "'`40bac966e410f1073d9a5bc1b0cb981315979970` foundation remains unchanged. No actual Twitch raid/chat, OAuth login, cloud operation, credential read or deployment was performed. Release health still says foundation/not-ready-for-raids; ownership transfer, two-chat claim, completed lineage/rings and arrival animations are not implemented.

A signed **broadcaster-only `!relic send @targetlogin`** command reserves one private bounded intent in the global registry and acknowledges promptly. A moderator badge never authorizes sending. No command-supplied ID is trusted. Source must hold the relic, and source/target must be explicitly configured, opted-in, online and unpaused/unbanned/unblocked. Commands predating current stream/consent or the send watermark are rejected. The target login must come from a trusted bounded lifecycle `logins` mapping; at most four channel/login entries are allowed. Reservation, event dedupe and lifecycle/mark context are one memory operation / Firestore transaction. No HTTP call is performed by the webhook.

`runtime.sendOff.processPending()` is an **explicit privileged service**, processing at most one intent per call. It uses the source broadcaster'"'s validated "'`streamer` OAuth role and existing `channel:manage:raids` grant, resolves the exact login with Get Users, verifies the returned ID/login against the reservation, and checks both authoritative stream IDs against Get Streams. Preflight GET 401 can refresh once before dispatch; failures are terminal preflight rejection. Immediately before POST, another store transaction rechecks the single holder, both consent/live/stream/pause/block conditions and lease ownership. HTTP calls never execute inside a transaction. Concurrent workers cannot cross the same dispatch boundary twice.

The shared 30-second worker lease and statuses survive process restart in Firestore (or across workers sharing the same memory instance). A two-minute queue expiry is safe only before dispatch. The worker persists **`dispatching` before Start Raid POST**. Exactly one POST can be issued for that intent: no retry on POST 401, timeout, 5xx, crash, lost response or database-finalization failure. A timeout/5xx yields **`unknown`**; an expired dispatch marker also becomes unknown on a subsequent explicit worker call. Unknown and accepted intents remain reconcile-only and block replacement sends. A crash after marking dispatch but before actually sending may therefore issue zero raids; this deliberate at-most-once policy prefers a stuck intent to duplicate raids. Definitive HTTP 4xx/preflight rejection terminates the intent and allows a fresh later owner command; this is never an automatic POST retry. Policy changes after the persisted dispatch boundary cannot atomically retract an external request already in flight.

**Bootstrap/worker wiring remains pending:** there is no automatic startup drain, post-response CPU loop, unauthenticated processing endpoint, background polling timer or authenticated operator worker UI supplied here. After reviewed account/subscription setup, a separately authenticated worker/control-plane integration must call `processPending()`. An event receipt alone cannot wake that worker in this increment. Unknown/accepted outcomes reconcile via a matching signed actual raid event; no unsafe clear-and-retry operator API is implemented. Missing confirmation requires investigation/a future reviewed reconciliation control, not an automatic repeat of Start Raid.

**One Keeper grant remains supported.** Runtime configuration still contains only the configured streamer, and its default login mapping only identifies the initial home. It does not pretend to authenticate/opt-in OlsOls2 or another destination. Two-channel configurations used in unit tests are synthetic internal fixtures. A real eligible destination needs explicit trusted mapping, authenticated opt-in, authoritative lifecycle delivery and future second-channel OAuth/routing/bootstrap work before this service is end-to-end usable. Non-Keeper/offline/unknown targets cannot reserve a relic send; the relic stays with its existing source.

### Signed actual raid is the only travel confirmation

The public webhook validates `channel.raid` type/version, exactly one incoming `to_broadcaster_user_id` or outgoing `from_broadcaster_user_id` condition bound to the configured channel, and the event'"'s from/to IDs. The explicit subscription manager now plans **five** subscriptions: online, offline, incoming raid, outgoing raid and chat. No startup subscription action occurs. A raw accepted Start Raid response is **not** travel and creates no ritual/hop.

In lifecycle-enabled stores, the old unconditional naked-raid ritual is disabled. Only an eligible signed raid from the current single holder to an opted-in live Keeper can atomically create "'`pendingHop` plus a local ritual with event dedupe. With an active send, its target, source/target stream IDs and event time must match the reservation/dispatch; unrelated, mismatched or stale raids cannot claim the relic. Matching unknown intent can be confirmed by the actual event without retrying the API. Without an active intent, an eligible manual raid can create the same pending-handoff foundation. Both channels are conservatively required online at confirmation; delivery after an observed source offline fails closed rather than inventing eligibility.

The ritual starts at **verified EventSub receipt time**, lasts **90 local seconds**, and is never synchronized with Twitch'"'s separate raid UX countdown. Registry metadata includes a short "'`snatchedUntil` marker and `phase:pending-handoff`; no animation or completed handoff is claimed. **Holder remains the source**. A future claim still requires incoming raiders AND host chat. An active pending hop cannot be overwritten; a signed event-time watermark prevents older events replacing a newer hop even after a previous window expires. No lineage rings are earned by an API call or by this pending transition.

The existing 4 KiB global-registry guard bounds one intent, one pending hop and scalar watermarks; there is no growing outbox/history. Existing channel/marks caps and approved-rune-only public projection remain. Intents, target login/IDs, worker lease and pending-hop details stay internal; no private fields or fabricated phase animation were added to the overlay. Fake transaction rollback/retry tests ensure reservation/event atomicity without running external effects.

Implemented the Send Off service and verified-raid foundations:
